title: HFCL shares locked in 5% lower circuit, down 21% in a month despite record Q2 profit: What lies ahead?

HFCL shares hit the 5% lower circuit despite record Q2 FY27 results, with net profit rising to ₹ 394.22 crore and revenue more than doubling. The company expects at least 80% FY27 revenue growth, backed by a ₹ 28,900 crore order book and planned ₹ 1,800 crore capacity investments. Dhanya Nagasundaram Published 9 Nov 2026, 12:32 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google HFCL shares locked in 5% lower circuit, down 21% in a month despite record Q2 profit ( Photo: AI generated ) AI Quick Read HFCL share price remained locked in the 5% lower circuit on Monday, 9 November, extending its recent decline despite the telecom equipment maker reporting its strongest-ever quarterly performance in Q2 FY27. The stock has fallen 6.23% over the past week and 15.73% in the last two weeks. It has declined 21.14% over the past month and 1.01% in the past three months. However, the stock continues to trade significantly higher, with gains of 45.98% over six months and 199.10% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The weakness comes despite a sharp improvement in the company's financial performance, with HFCL reporting a multi-fold increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter, supported by strong demand for optical fibre cables from artificial intelligence (AI) data centres. The company has also outlined an ambitious growth outlook, backed by a sizeable order book and planned investments to expand manufacturing capacity. Record quarterly performance HFCL reported a multi-fold jump in consolidated net profit to ₹ 394.22 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with approximately ₹ 72 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its regulatory filing. Consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled to ₹ 2,541.79 crore during the quarter, from ₹ 1,043.34 crore in the year-ago period. The company's profit after tax (PAT) margin also expanded sharply to 14.36% from 2.23% a year earlier. The strong performance was driven by rising demand for optical fibre cables, particularly from AI data centres, alongside growing opportunities across telecom networks and data centre infrastructure. Calling it the best-ever quarterly performance in HFCL's history, Managing Director Mahendra Nahata said the results reflected the growing scale, strength and momentum of the business. He added that the performance reinforced the company's confidence in delivering sustained growth and creating long-term value for stakeholders. Ambitious growth targets Building on the strong quarterly performance, HFCL has raised its growth ambitions, projecting revenue growth of at least 80% in FY27 compared with FY26. Nahata said the company's order book exceeds ₹ 28,900 crore, providing multi-year revenue visibility. Beyond its secured orders, HFCL also has a strong pipeline of opportunities at advanced stages of conversion. Demand is accelerating across AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centres and telecom networks, while opportunities with international hyperscalers and telecom operators are increasingly translating into firm contracts, he said. The company had earlier targeted achieving ₹ 10,000 crore in revenue by FY29. However, supported by the current business momentum, management now believes it could reach the milestone significantly ahead of schedule. ₹ 1,800 crore capacity expansion To support its growth ambitions, HFCL plans to invest approximately ₹ 1,800 crore across optical fibre, cable and preform manufacturing. The investment is aimed at expanding production capacity, strengthening backward integration and improving its position in the growing data centre connectivity market. Nahata said the company's advanced optical fibre cable portfolio and data centre connectivity solutions continue to strengthen its competitive position as demand for digital infrastructure expands. Also Read | Divi's Laboratories shares hit record high rising 84% YTD; buy, sell or hold? Defence and aerospace: Next growth driver Beyond its telecom and optical fibre businesses, HFCL is looking to build its defence and aerospace operations into another major growth engine. Its defence portfolio includes thermal weapon sights, electronic fuzes, surveillance radars, Multi-Mode Hand Grenades and aerostructures. Nahata said the ongoing acquisition of the aerospace business is expected to be completed during the current quarter, further strengthening the company's capabilities and presence in the sector. HFCL remains on track to achieve its target of approximately ₹ 500 crore in defence revenue in FY27, he added. With a sizeable order book, rising demand from AI data centres and an expanding defence portfolio, HFCL is positioning itself for its next phase of growth. However, the sharp correction in its share price, despite record quarterly earnings and an upbeat outlook, puts investor focus on the sustainability of its rally and the company's ability to convert its order pipeline into revenue and profitability. HFCL share price today HFCL share price today opened at an intraday high of ₹ 213.50 apiece on the BSE, the stock touched an intraday low of ₹ 206.05 apiece. Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said HFCL has been forming potential bull-trap patterns on the weekly chart. He noted that the stock has repeatedly made higher highs during breakout attempts but failed to sustain those levels, subsequently slipping lower and trapping buyers. Arora said the stock was down 5% and trading near a crucial support level of ₹ 200. A decisive break below this level could trigger further weakness, initially towards the ₹ 160–165 demand zone. The stock could also fill the price gap around ₹ 178–180 during the decline, he added. Rajesh Bhosale, Technical Analyst at My Advisor Alpha, said HFCL has witnessed a sharp correction over the past couple of weeks and is now approaching a crucial support level of ₹ 200, which coincides with its previous swing low. Bhosale cautioned that a break below ₹ 200 could lead to further downside towards ₹ 175. On the upside, ₹ 215 remains the immediate resistance level to watch, he said.
